notes.title: Choose where representatives handle conversations
notes.body:
Start with the representative’s working environment. Copilot Service workspace brings customer sessions and CRM context into one representative-facing application. Its separate sessions preserve the context of concurrent interactions. A representative needs the Omnichannel Agent role to use it.

When a team must remain in a non-Microsoft CRM, consider the embedded conversation widget. The Salesforce setup connects the widget through a call-center definition and softphone utility. Its adapter URL must point to the embedded widget, not to a customer-facing chat script.

These are workspace decisions within a broader contact-center implementation. Validate channel provisioning and the chosen integration’s prerequisites before rollout. A familiar CRM screen does not remove the need to configure the underlying contact-center service.

notes.title: Move configuration without losing deployment control
notes.body:
Keep the configuration’s source of truth in development. Microsoft recommends authoring in an unmanaged solution, then exporting it as managed for the destination. Check installed solution-version parity first. Direct changes to imported managed records create an active layer that can hide later managed updates.

A channel migration also has dependencies. Prepare referenced custom schema and appropriate migration permissions. Inspect the documented migration scope instead of assuming that every connected service setting travels with the channel.

Environment recovery is a separate operation. After a reset, restore, or tenant move, follow the documented channel provisioning or unified-routing enablement steps. Include a functional conversation check in the rollout plan; an environment being available is not the same as its contact-center configuration being ready.

notes.title: Distinguish authenticated customers from matching records
notes.body:
Customer identification and authentication solve different problems. Preconversation answers can locate a contact or account, but a supplied email address is not proof that the visitor owns that identity. If identification finds several matching records, the system does not automatically link one arbitrarily.

Authenticated chat instead uses a signed token from the website’s sign-in flow. Configure the authentication record and associate it with the chat channel instance. Creating the record alone does not wire it into that widget.

For a support portal, review both outcomes: is the visitor authenticated, and is the intended customer record linked? Treat them as separate acceptance checks. The source documents specific record-search conditions; do not infer that every custom field or status value participates in automatic matching.

notes.title: Collect chat context and deploy the correct widget
notes.body:
A preconversation survey collects information before chat begins. Its internal question name and its customer-facing wording serve different purposes. Adding a question creates a corresponding workstream context variable; the displayed sentence is not a substitute for that variable’s identifier.

Use stable context names consistently across integrations. Names are case-sensitive. Before changing or removing a variable, check whether routing rules depend on it. Context can also support representative tools such as scripts and macros.

Finally, deploy the customer-facing widget from the intended chat instance. For a conventional website, copy its snippet into the page body; a Power Apps portal uses its Chat Widget Code content snippet. Test the actual customer page so that survey configuration, widget selection, and collected context are checked together.

notes.title: Give representatives the right Copilot assistance
notes.body:
Start with the task: finding a knowledge-based answer and recapping a conversation are different needs. Configure the help pane for questions; configure conversation summaries for a recap. Then enable the appropriate features in the representatives’ experience profile rather than assuming global setup gives every group identical access.

Custom security roles also need the documented Copilot privileges.

For standalone Contact Center, conversation summaries can cover chat and transcribed voice. An administrator can trigger them when someone joins, at the end, or on demand. Representatives can copy a summary or give feedback; creating a case from it additionally requires case management and the enabled action.

For example, a consultation needs a useful recap, while a product-policy question needs suitable published knowledge. Validate both workflows with the intended profile.

notes.title: Scope voice-agent variables before sharing context
notes.body:
For the native standalone integration, a context variable and its Copilot Studio counterpart need matching names and compatible types. A global variable is accessible across topics in one user session; it is not a permanent customer record. Use a Set variable value node when the agent must assign a value itself.

For external values, enable the global and external-source usage settings. Keep the channel’s limitations explicit: Contact Center IVR does not support the external-variable timeout setting described for other scenarios. Do not design voice recovery around that timer.

For example, retain a caller’s selected service category across topics, then pass the relevant context at escalation. This transfers conversation context, not proof that an arbitrary value authenticates the caller.

notes.title: Separate work enrichment from representative assignment
notes.body:
Classification enriches a work item; assignment selects an eligible representative. Keep these responsibilities visible when troubleshooting. A useful classification attribute can be reused by queue-routing or prioritization rules, instead of repeating the same business test in several places.

Ruleset order matters. Classification runs before route-to-queue evaluation, and a later classification ruleset can consume an earlier ruleset’s output. Within one classification ruleset, a matching item passes processing to the next ruleset.

For example, derive an urgency category once, then use it downstream. Separately inspect the queue’s assignment method and representative eligibility. A classification result does not mean that a suitable representative is immediately available; automated assignment retries when it cannot find one.

notes.title: Treat skill eligibility and workload limits separately
notes.body:
An exact skill match requires the attached skills at sufficient proficiency. With standard assignment, presence and available capacity also matter. A queue using custom assignment needs its own skill conditions; the workstream’s default skill algorithm does not supply those conditions automatically.

Capacity profiles describe workload limits. Assignment blocking can stop further automatic work when a profile reaches its limit, even if another profile has room. A supervisor’s manual assignment can exceed configured capacity, so the limit is not an absolute ban on every assignment path.

For example, an unassigned language-specific conversation calls for an eligibility check, while unexpected extra manually assigned work calls for a capacity-path check. Do not treat these as the same fault.

notes.title: Build a session from reusable templates
notes.body:
Scope: Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone in Copilot Service workspace.

A session template determines the anchor application, additional tabs, and initial communication-panel mode. The anchor remains available throughout the session. Create custom templates instead of editing supplied templates.

Application tab templates describe the pages to open. A third-party website tab requires a site that permits iframe hosting; a valid URL alone is insufficient. Associate the needed tabs with the session template, then connect that session experience to the workstream.

For a troubleshooting checklist, separate three questions: Which session template is selected? Which application tabs does it reference? Can each target page load in the chosen page type? Test these relationships with a representative conversation.

notes.title: Separate guidance, automation, and session context
notes.body:
Scope: Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone in Copilot Service workspace.

Scripts guide a representative through a process; a step can show an instruction, run a macro, or open another script. An expression on the session template can choose a default script from those associated with that session.

Macros execute configured actions in sequence. Begin with Start macro execution. For reusable automation, resolve context through supported parameters rather than hard-coding a customer's identity. The automation dictionary supplies runtime values; use the documented format for the particular context.

Check what each action actually commits. Autofill form fields changes the form; add a save action when the workflow must explicitly persist those values rather than waiting for autosave.

notes.title: Choose a supervisor intervention and the right access
notes.body:
Scope: Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone, with voice and supervisor capabilities configured.

For a voice call, monitoring lets a supervisor observe without appearing as a participant. Private messages can guide the representative without showing the message to the customer. Joining the call is a different intervention: the supervisor speaks in the conversation and the representative is notified. The documented role for these voice operations is Omnichannel Supervisor.

Analytics access is a separate configuration concern. A custom reporting role needs applicable report-table and underlying data read privileges. Editing analytics reports uses the Analytics Report Author role. Decide whether the person needs to inspect a live interaction, read dashboards, or author reports before choosing permissions.

notes.title: Move from operational metrics to conversation evidence
notes.body:
Real-time reports help a supervisor inspect current operations. In a standalone voice-enabled contact center, the voice analytics option adds voice insights. A missing option can reflect missing voice configuration rather than a report-layout problem.

For event-level investigation, conversation diagnostics stores lifecycle data in Azure Application Insights. Configuration requires a Managed environment and the documented Azure and Power Platform permissions. Inspect the relevant event: classification and queue selection are different stages.

The Diagnose dashboard can compare requirements against a representative's presence, capacity, and skills at an assignment attempt. Its diagnostic insights are documented for out-of-the-box assignment methods. Do not extend that limitation to all raw telemetry: the event documentation also describes custom assignment ruleset details.

notes.title: Control rollout separately from agent configuration
notes.body:
Agent hub brings adoption guidance, rollout management and agent performance information together. Use it to organize a controlled introduction of AI capabilities, rather than treating every agent setting as one global switch. Its guidance also covers security, architecture and privacy considerations.

The rollout manager works with agent configurations that already exist. Enable the autonomous agents before creating a plan, then follow the wizard for the selected agents and business scope. A plan can cover one agent or several, and Schedule can enable the plan at a future date and time. Individual agent settings remain on their corresponding administration pages.

Plan lifecycle actions have different effects by agent. Deactivating or deleting a Customer Intent Agent or Customer Knowledge Management Agent plan leaves the corresponding agent setting intact. For Case Management Agent, those plan actions also deactivate or delete the associated rules. Before stopping a rollout, identify the selected agent and check the relevant settings or rules afterward. Do not assume that a plan disappearing means every underlying capability has stopped.

notes.title: Design a simulation that the preview can actually run
notes.body:
Agentic simulation is a preview capability for testing configurations, agents and routing before rollout. Its documented scope is inbound voice workstreams in English; it does not support DTMF menu interaction and is not intended for production use. These limits matter when deciding whether a proposed test can validate a complete journey.

Prepare the documented administrator roles, provision voice and configure the destination phone number for simulation. Launch the Agentic Simulation tile in Copilot Service admin center and describe the test in a natural-language prompt. Supply the number belonging to the workstream that should receive the call. The simulation supplies its own caller number; that is not the destination to put in the prompt.

Watch running calls in the Ongoing conversation report. Afterward, inspect run status and the submitted prompt in Simulation Run History, then use the closed conversation form for transcripts and recordings. Configure representatives and routing realistically before testing. A completed run is useful evidence about the supported journey you exercised; it cannot establish that an unsupported keypad branch works.

notes.title: Use conversational setup within its supported boundaries
notes.body:
Service Operations Agent helps Contact Center administrators configure, inspect and validate the environment using natural language in English. It can manage common components such as queues and workstreams. The conversational interface assists an administrator; it does not remove the need to understand the change being made.

For access, Microsoft specifies the Omnichannel administrator role. Managing Power Apps and MCP connections requires System Administrator. The prerequisites also include consumption-based billing; troubleshooting during setup requires Application Insights configured and connected. Conversational setup needs a Dataverse connection through the MCP server. Check this connection when the agent cannot retrieve information or perform supported actions.

Tool support has boundaries. The documented tools can create route-to-queue rules without conditions, but adding or editing rule conditions is a manual Copilot Service admin center task. Custom assignment and several other ruleset types also fall outside these tools. Provide precise names and channel context, review proposed changes and verify the resulting configuration. If an operation is unsupported, use its manual administration path instead of repeatedly rephrasing a prompt or escalating permissions without evidence.

notes.title: Prepare a representative account for real work
notes.body:
Treat onboarding as several checks. Create the regular human account in Microsoft 365, then verify that it is enabled and eligible for the intended Dataverse environment. Where an environment security group is used, check membership. Do not confuse appearing in the user list with being allowed to use its data: environment security roles are a separate requirement.

Next check the Contact Center duties. Basic User is required for Contact Center users, while the task-specific roles depend on what the person will do. Working with cases adds its own Customer Service Representative requirement. Use the documented role matrix rather than assuming that one familiar role covers every feature.

Finally prepare routing-related user settings. A human representative needs a bookable resource for unified routing. Default presence controls their initial status when signing in to the workspace. Enhanced user management can update existing skills, queues and capacity profiles in bulk. A useful rollout check follows one representative from sign-in through receiving an appropriate work item; it tests several layers that an account-creation check alone misses.

notes.title: Separate role privileges, personas and application access
notes.body:
Begin custom-role design with the user's tasks. Copy a suitable existing Contact Center role, then review its privileges and access levels. Preserve the minimum access needed for those tasks, including the required persona privilege. The mapping uses the admin, supervisor or agent archetype; it is not a reason to make every user a system administrator.

Role assignments combine. Adding a narrower custom role does not cancel a broader permission already supplied by another assigned role. A least-privilege review must therefore examine the user's whole set of role grants, not just the newly created role.

After mapping a custom role to a persona, check application, form and dashboard access separately. Persona mapping does not automatically grant those surfaces. For example, if the user has the intended privileges and persona but the application is unavailable, inspect that application's permitted roles before changing routing or adding broad administrative access.

notes.title: Change capacity settings without surprising existing work
notes.body:
Capacity profiles describe workload limits and are assigned to representatives who have bookable resources. Keep the profile's default limit separate from a representative-specific custom limit. A custom value governs that representative until it is cleared; changing the profile default does not replace it.

Configuration changes do not necessarily alter work already assigned. A lower custom limit affects new assignments without redistributing the representative's current work. Reset frequency is a different decision: changing it requires recreating the profile. Plan that change and its user associations rather than treating it as an ordinary limit edit.

notes.title: Separate chat routing from widget rollout
notes.body:
Start by choosing Messaging and Chat for the workstream. It owns routing and assignment behavior; the widget is the customer-facing entry point. Multiple chat channels may share that workstream, so plan shared routing deliberately.

For an existing classic channel, adding Modern UI preserves the workstream configuration. Test with the version-specific testing script. The general script follows whichever version is active, so changing that selection is a release decision, not just a preview action. Confirm the intended version on a test page before switching the live channel.

notes.title: Plan proactive invitations around customer choice
notes.body:
For Contact Center standalone, first enable proactive chat on the widget and ensure the target page embeds it. The visitor receives an invitation and can decline it; the representative notification follows acceptance.

Choose a meaningful trigger separately from the invitation wording. The developer example uses elapsed time after widget readiness. Supply the message through notificationUIConfig and choose showPrechat intentionally if the widget has a survey. Test the accept and decline paths as well as the trigger itself; an invitation is not an already accepted service conversation.

notes.title: Publish quick replies for the right audience
notes.body:
Treat language and audience as separate checks. Write a separate response for each locale; selecting a locale does not translate its text. Associate departmental replies with the relevant workstreams. A reply without an association is broadly available, subject to language settings.

Then check the representative experience. Administrator-created responses appear on All, while personal responses appear on Personal when that feature is enabled. Before duplicating an apparently missing response, check the tab, language and workstream. This keeps a useful shared response from becoming several separately maintained personal copies.

notes.title: Connect the SMS account, workstream and provider callback
notes.body:
For the documented US-number Twilio setup, provision the channel and prepare the provider subscription and secure-column permissions. Register its credentials and number, then configure an SMS workstream.

Complete the provider connection by placing the workstream inbound URL in that number's Twilio Messaging settings. Credential validation alone does not demonstrate incoming delivery. For rollout, test an actual customer message through to the representative; configure opt-out handling with the provider.

notes.title: Prepare translation logic before enabling the conversation setting
notes.body:
In the documented web-resource configuration, prepare the translation service and customize its JavaScript integration before enabling translation. Upload and publish the script as a web resource, then register its URL in the translation settings and choose the representative input language. The script and service provide the translation logic; the toggle is only part of setup.

For Azure Translation Services, the administration guide specifies the global endpoint. If isolated messages keep switching the detected customer language, the documented history-based detection option stabilizes that choice. This note describes the published web-resource workflow, rather than inferring delivery from a release-plan date.

notes.title: Check the dependencies behind customer location and self-service history
notes.body:
Customer context has separate dependencies. The documented visitor-location integration is restricted to existing Bing Maps for Enterprise customers through June 30, 2028; new customers and Azure Maps customers cannot use that feature. For an eligible deployment, create a provider with its Bing key and associate it with the widget. The visitor must also allow the browser location request.

For standalone Contact Center, self-service history needs portal code that supplies the customer's earlier actions as context. Enable Self service under Customer Settings after that integration exists. A visible tab alone is not evidence that the portal is capturing useful history.

notes.title: Preserve CRM identity while designing synchronization
notes.body:
Connect the source CRM and Dataverse in the intended environment. The documented connector needs matching Power Apps and Power Automate environments, plus Source CRM, Source CRM ID and Source CRM URL columns on account and contact records. These preserve where a synchronized record came from.

Plan initial loading separately from ongoing changes. A manual initial load may need pagination; incremental triggers or webhooks carry later create, update and delete events. Test a changed source record as well as an initial import before considering the integration ready.

notes.title: Separate embedded desktop setup from retained-provider responsibilities
notes.body:
For Salesforce embedding, importing the call-center definition is only one part of setup. Add the intended user to that call center, configure a default softphone layout and add the Open CTI Softphone utility to the Service Console. Validate the representative experience with that user.

Microsoft also documents an architecture that retains both an existing CRM and CCaaS provider while adding Copilot assistance. In that specific architecture, existing providers still handle routing, follow-up and supervision. An assistance component should not be mistaken for replacement of those operational services.

notes.title: Plan channel migration dependencies and managed cleanup
notes.body:
Build a channel migration checklist before exporting records. The documented sequence moves session and notification templates, skill rules, new capacity profiles and queues before channel workstreams/settings. The channel procedure excludes account, provider, agent and AI/analytics setup, so assign separate work for those dependencies.

Treat cleanup as a managed lifecycle operation. Imported managed configuration cannot simply be deleted as a target record; Microsoft directs removal through the supplying managed solution. Assess that solution’s contents and dependencies before removal so cleanup does not unintentionally remove other configuration.

notes.title: Revalidate target integrations after an omnichannel environment copy
notes.body:
A full environment copy carries integration configuration, not proof that the target can safely serve users. Review target accounts, numbers, agents and websites, then test routing and escalation. Record-routing configuration needs separate target configuration and validation. Replace a website’s source chat snippet with the generated target snippet.

For ACS voice, the copy guidance requires a target-specific resource and number rather than sharing the source resource. Plan disconnection carefully: the disconnection procedure releases associated numbers from Dynamics 365 and calls for Event Grid subscription cleanup. Validate target agent connections and publish the intended agent before testing it.

notes.title: Prepare records before expecting automatic assignment
notes.body:
For record-based unified routing, enable the table for queues before configuring its routing. In table properties, select Can be added to a queue. Treat that as a design decision: the option cannot subsequently be disabled. Also inspect automatic movement into the owner's default queue; that option prevents automatic distribution to representatives.

Then prepare the routing chain: enable unified routing, configure representative resources and advanced queues, enable the record for routing and create its record workstream. Use Save & Route on a test case to exercise the runtime path. Creating a record through an email rule and distributing that record are separate operations; validate the actual assignment, not merely successful record creation.

notes.title: Choose an integration surface before writing channel code
notes.body:
Choose by where the integration runs. For mobile apps, Microsoft recommends the native iOS/Android Messaging SDKs, with authenticated persistent chat for returning users. The SDK provides a ready interface or lifecycle functions for a bespoke one, plus push-notification support. A WebView is an alternative with documented feature and performance limitations.

For a website widget, use the Live Chat Widget SDK. A startChat customContext argument takes precedence over a previously configured context provider. For a backend-owned custom channel, use Messaging APIs instead of invoking confidential-client REST calls directly from customer devices. Register the Entra app, tenant and HTTPS webhook, then connect the channel record to a messaging workstream and routing.

For an existing ACS-based WhatsApp deployment, channel registration, its Event Grid callback and workstream association are separate integration steps. Microsoft supports affected ACS configurations through September 30, 2028 and recommends WhatsApp through Twilio as the long-term path. Inventory templates and integrations before migration, obtain provider approval where required, and test inbound and outbound messaging. Verify provider coverage and number-migration requirements before procurement.

notes.title: Manage conversation state separately from representative availability
notes.body:
Automatic closure depends on both channel and state. Ordinary live chat in Active has no default automatic closure. Waiting inactivity is configured on the workstream for persistent chat, SMS, social and Teams; it is not a universal timer for every live chat. Closure eligibility is evaluated by a scheduler, and conversation activity can recalculate the timer. Use supported settings rather than manually patching conversation state/status records.

Representative availability is another layer. A custom presence has a base state and display text; Allowed Presences in the workstream uses the base state. Make the label agree with its routing meaning.

During a conversation, consult when private assistance is needed. The primary representative must separately add a consultant to include them with the customer. Transfer hands the work item to another representative or queue and removes the original representative after completion. Where enabled, reroute returns the conversation to system routing instead of selecting a colleague directly.

notes.title: Configure text protection and attachment permissions independently
notes.body:
For automated text masking in chat and asynchronous messaging, define and test the regular expression, keep its rule Active and select the sender direction to which it applies. Test representative-originated and customer-originated messages separately. The customer-to-representative masking option hides async customer data in the representative UI; do not promise it hides the original on the sender's device. Manual masking is a distinct feature, and removing text from a voice transcript does not erase retained audio.

Attachments have independent permissions for customers and representatives. Check the channel's supported file types, the configured size limit and blocked extensions as well as the direction toggle. A permission switch cannot expand the provider's format support. Files already attached to a transferred conversation remain accessible to the receiving representative.

notes.title: Test automated messages and the enhanced conversation form in their actual scope
notes.body:
Automated messages respond to events, while quick replies are selected by a representative. Set the shared channel-level message first, then create instance-specific text only where an account or number needs an exception. An instance customization overrides that channel-level setting. For supported messaging contexts, use the exact context variable name in {$VariableName$}; missing variables produce an empty value. Context placeholders are not supported in voice messages. Verify messages during live conversations because they are not included in the customer chat transcript.

The enhanced Contact Center Active Conversation form provides the Customer 360 component. Customize the relevant account/contact card in Power Apps. The form selector for open/closed conversations is hidden by default; enabling Show Conversation form selector is a separate setting-definition change. App-specific values override the environment value. Save and publish customizations, and keep the initial form light by moving less-used controls to secondary tabs.

notes.title: Separate timeline extension from telephony integration
notes.body:
Configure the timeline on the table form that representatives actually use. Choose the activities, notes and posts it should display, then save and publish. A custom activity table must use the Activity type to appear as an activity.

For another record source, a timeline custom connector is a JavaScript web resource implementing IRecordSource. This is not merely a Power Automate connector registration. Configure its resource and constructor on the timeline and keep client resources free of tokens and secrets. When moving the form in a solution, add those web resources explicitly: the configured references are not automatically exported as formal dependencies.

For third-party telephony in the multisession workspace, evaluate Channel Integration Framework 2.0 instead. CIF1 targets single-session apps; CIF2 hosts telephony providers and supports multisession templates and multiple providers. Timeline connectors supply record entries, whereas CIF connects a communication provider to the representative desktop.

notes.title: Publish customer-feedback surveys before attaching them to channels
notes.body:
Create a feedback survey from Customer settings in Copilot Service admin center. Copilot Studio and the channel must be in the same environment, and the administrator needs the Omnichannel administrator role. Check the Dataverse connection reference, customize the agent in Copilot Studio and publish it. Ready is different from merely having created the survey.

Attach the published survey to the channel's post-conversation configuration, selecting Powered by Microsoft Copilot Studio for digital messaging. When extending the survey with stored questions, use response variable names beginning MCS_. Keep changes within the supported Conversation Start topic.

An environment copy is not a complete survey deployment: Microsoft recommends creating new survey agents in the target because copied agents do not work as expected. Test a real conversation ending and the resulting response record rather than relying only on a preview link.

notes.title: Choose the telephony model before configuring numbers
notes.body:
Begin with the telephony architecture, carrier requirements and existing investments. Teams Phone extensibility uses Teams resource accounts and synchronized service numbers; create and associate the account, satisfy its licensing and consent prerequisites, then sync the number into a voice workstream. It is a different setup from separately provisioning standalone ACS telephony.

Current migration guidance identifies Teams Phone extensibility as the destination for affected standalone ACS voice deployments before September 30, 2028. Existing affected services remain supported during the transition. Retaining a carrier and SBC can favor Teams Direct Routing; other requirements may favor Operator Connect or Calling Plans. Inventory dependencies and pilot the target before scheduling a production cutover.

notes.title: Connect a usable number to the inbound workstream
notes.body:
For the documented ACS number-management path, check resource eligibility, regional availability and number capabilities before acquisition or import. New-ACS-customer acquisition restrictions in the transition guidance mean the older acquisition wizard is not a universal new-deployment recommendation.

Inbound setup needs a provisioned voice channel, unified routing and an inbound-capable number. Create a Voice workstream, associate the number, and configure language, behaviors and routing. The picker excludes numbers already bound elsewhere. Releasing a number is a separate destructive administration action: first remove workstream/outbound-profile associations and disable personal assignment where applicable. Test the intended incoming call path before considering the configuration ready.

notes.title: Preserve external IVR context through a scoped integration
notes.body:
The documented non-Microsoft IVR integration uses ACS Direct Routing: connect the IVR's SBC to the ACS resource, register its number and send a SIP INVITE for the transfer. SIP UUI carries key/value context. Define matching workstream context variables with exactly the parameter names used in that payload.

Call arrival and useful context are separate validation checks. The external IVR's own recording and transcript are not made available to the representative by this integration. Review SBC connectivity and the boundary where SIP information leaves the Microsoft network; do not assume a PSTN handoff preserves every header. Apply this ACS-specific procedure within the published transition plan rather than treating it as the Teams Phone provisioning workflow.

notes.title: Separate direct inward dialing from queue-based voice routing
notes.body:
Inbound profiles serve personal direct inward dialing, whereas workstreams route inbound conversations through queues. Direct inward calls do not use unified routing and are not tracked in its historical routing analytics. Choose the path that matches the operating model before interpreting missing routing metrics.

For outbound calling, prepare a number that supports Make calls, a voice queue, capacity and the outbound profile. Add representatives to the capacity profile used by that outbound profile. Configure caller ID and call behaviors there; the dialer number label is not customer-facing CNAM. A representative's general inbound readiness does not establish outbound-profile membership.

notes.title: Treat voice capture as a chain of prerequisites
notes.body:
In the documented ACS recording flow, tenant-level audio controls can prevent workstream recording. Check the allowed audio/MPEG MIME types and Event Grid system-topic registration as well as the workstream Behaviors setting. Choose transcription alone or transcription with recording and select automatic or manual start. Consent and applicable organizational requirements still need their own review.

Translated voice transcripts require the recording, transcription and real-time translation features described by the administration guide. Copilot Studio's agent transcript is a separate artifact; a DTMF-only agent ignores spoken input and captures keypad entries instead. For sensitive external interactions, inspect the contact-specific secure settings as well: preview overrides can stop audio only or both audio and transcript capture even where the workstream normally records.

notes.title: Collect representative feedback and verify secure transfer behavior
notes.body:
The representative call-quality survey measures the representative's experience after a call, rather than customer satisfaction. Enable it in Voice call experiences and choose its frequency. Configure the Azure Monitor Call Survey Logs diagnostic setting to a supported destination so responses are retained; displaying a survey alone does not ensure storage.

Transfer behavior also needs explicit testing. In enhanced voice, bridging normally continues the original call and its capture, while unbridged transfer starts a new call with different capture and DTMF behavior. The DTMF-broadcast setting and secure external-contact preview settings add further conditions. Where secure settings apply, test the chosen contact's audio/transcription and hold policy rather than inferring it only from the workstream defaults.

notes.title: Separate SDK responsibilities from the business cost model
notes.body:
In Microsoft's CCaaS Teams Phone extensibility architecture, the server handles incoming-call notifications and answers through Call Automation. The representative client uses the Calling SDK. Adding a participant and transferring are server-side control decisions; the overview recommends AddParticipant rather than Redirect when adding CCaaS agents. This is verified architectural guidance, not a complete Dynamics-specific SDK reference.

Cost planning should then reflect the proposed design. Include named-user licensing, AI/telephony consumption, retained infrastructure and integration maintenance. Measure expected changes in interaction volume, handling time, employee experience and quality instead of assuming that license consolidation proves savings. Compare those assumptions with a pilot and current commercial terms; a single per-user price cannot establish the total cost.

notes.title: Build outbound engagement around identity and contact preferences
notes.body:
Start with provisioned channels and choose how customer records enter the engagement: file, API or an enabled Customer Insights journey. Configure the outbound workstream and engagement's queue, skills and identity key. A stable external contact identifier should map to the selected eligible Contact attribute so repeated imports update the same person. Review generated routing rather than maintaining unrelated parallel rules.

Before delivery, configure quiet hours, frequency and opt-outs. Customer-local evaluation needs the timezone supplied in the input; the system does not infer it from a phone number. Technical implicit opt-in is not evidence of legally required consent. Test suppressed contacts alongside ordinary deliveries, and use the channel-specific consent records when honoring a do-not-contact request.

notes.title: Choose dial behavior for the intended service experience
notes.body:
Preview, progressive, predictive and Copilot modes make different tradeoffs. Preview notifies a representative first and supports reviewing the customer before the call; manual or delayed start is specific to the documented Teams Phone extensibility setup. In the documented ACS preview path, the call starts after acceptance.

Progressive uses available representatives to pace calls; predictive adjusts dialing against capacity and performance; Copilot starts with an AI agent and escalates when needed. Treat these as operational choices, not blanket permission to automate any campaign. The dial-mode article restricts specified automated modes for commercial marketing/sales and flags telecommunications compliance concerns. Review purpose, consent and applicable requirements before use, then validate the representative and customer experience with a small service-outreach pilot.

notes.title: Enable outbound monitoring before interpreting campaign results
notes.body:
A configured engagement does not automatically establish dashboard access. Enable real-time analytics for proactive engagement and give the operator the documented Omnichannel Supervisor role. Open the Proactive Engagement dashboard and use its engagement, queue, timezone and business-unit filters to establish the scope of the view.

Read metrics by their definitions. Pending work has not yet been attempted; in-progress deliveries are active; throughput measures deliveries processed over the last hour. A completed delivery has reached a final intended outcome, which can include the end of attempts, so it is not interchangeable with a live-person connection. Use connect rate and live-person measures when the operational question is whether outreach actually reaches people.

notes.title: Establish workforce scope and access before planning
notes.body:
Install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package, then prepare the relevant users and planning scope. Copilot Service workspace continues to use its Omnichannel roles. The separate Workforce Engagement Management app is preview and introduces dedicated roles; a WFM Forecaster can manage forecasts without permission to publish schedules. Assign roles for the surface and duties actually used.

Define planning groups around queue/channel demand, timezone and service objectives. The group links forecast, capacity and shift plans so staffing assumptions stay aligned. A queue/channel combination belongs to only one planning group at a time, preventing duplicated demand. This staffing scope differs from a representative's per-conversation capacity profile: one plans required coverage, while the other constrains assignment workload.

notes.title: Turn historical demand into a reproducible staffing input
notes.body:
A forecast scenario defines entity, channels, queues, timezone and history, then predicts interaction volume and average handle time. A capacity plan uses forecast demand and service objectives to estimate staffing. When a planning group is selected, its timezone and demand fields populate the scenario and become read-only, keeping plans aligned.

For an external data source, upload history before scenario creation and plan a deliberate refresh process: automatic refresh is unavailable for that source. Saving a scenario does not prove a successful run. Check job history, inspect output, and use a new snapshot where supported to reflect updated history. Validate the input scope and run status before interpreting an unexpected staffing result; this is demand planning, not a decision about an individual employee.

notes.title: Publish schedules and synchronize external workforce data deliberately
notes.body:
Build a shift plan from the required skills, queues, calendar and activity itinerary, using a capacity plan when forecast-based coverage is required. Schedule representatives, inspect the resulting board, then publish the selected schedule. Editing a committed booking returns it to Unpublished, so republish the change rather than assuming the representative already sees the update.

If another workforce tool remains authoritative, use a defined Dataverse API integration for schedules and assignments, and provide operational data back to that tool where needed. Establish service-to-service authentication, data ownership, synchronization frequency and error handling. Schedule imports and real-time adherence have different freshness needs. Handle rate limits and transient failures with backoff; increasing request rate during throttling risks making the integration less reliable.

notes.title: Test AI delays and failures as part of the customer journey
notes.body:
Give the customer an initial greeting before beginning a potentially slow data lookup. Configure an appropriate latency message and examine connector or flow performance rather than leaving silence unexplained. Design retries, alternative paths and representative escalation for failed or incomplete tool responses.

For commitments or sensitive actions, prompts alone are insufficient enforcement. Use deterministic controls and the required human approval path. Test the full workflow under realistic telephony, background-noise, language and tool-failure conditions, then monitor latency, task completion and escalation after rollout. A successful demonstration of the happy path does not establish reliability across all callers or operating conditions.

notes.title: Ground answers and summaries in the intended information
notes.body:
Configure the help pane for the information task, not just its visibility. For organizational knowledge, enable the knowledge-source option and maintain the latest published article version in the representative UI language. Check the feature/source matrix: the documented external-web-resource option is not an Ask a question source. Copilot Studio knowledge is a separate supported source path.

For Customer Service case summaries, review the included source fields and remove irrelevant notification content with Specify information to exclude. Test both a policy question and a noisy case summary; correct access alone does not establish that the selected material is relevant.

notes.title: Extend assistance and interpret adoption separately from quality
notes.body:
The current Customer Service extensibility procedure enables Extend agent with Copilot Studio, then opens the linked managed agent to configure tools and knowledge. Tools can retrieve structured data or perform actions. Pass relevant custom context deliberately, and respect the managed-agent restrictions. The article labels this a production-ready preview.

Use the standalone Copilot analytics report to examine adoption with consistent duration and timezone filters. A response counted as used was copied; that does not prove it was correct or resolved the issue. Combine usage with response ratings and operational investigation rather than treating a copy count as a quality score.

notes.title: Build smart assist as a custom representative assistant
notes.body:
Separate custom smart assist from customer-facing self-service. The documented development route uses Azure Bot Service. Create its application user with the Omnichannel agent role, enable the productivity pane and smart assist, then add that user in the workstream’s Smart assist bots area. Copilot Studio agents are not supported as these assistants.

Validate timing as well as registration: recommendations appear after the representative sends a message. The administration article also warns that built-in case and knowledge suggestions stopped being supported in June2025. Do not assume a legacy sample establishes support for those retired built-ins.

notes.title: Choose an IVR execution model and define its input paths
notes.body:
For a predefined menu, Basic voice with classic orchestration offers explicit topic and trigger-phrase control. For generative orchestration, follow the Real-time voice configuration instead. Voice authoring alone does not activate Telephony; provision the phone/channel and associate the agent with its voice workstream.

Specify what each topic receives and returns. In a real-time hybrid flow, only declared output variables return to the model as structured data. For keypad navigation, map the Question nodes carefully: a matching local key or multi-digit question consumes input before a global DTMF command. Test speech intent and keypad paths independently.

notes.title: Design separate controls for sensitive data and recording consent
notes.body:
Mark sensitive collected variables in Question nodes and use deterministic handling for sensitive-data flows. Masking protects supported transcripts/logs; it does not stop persistence in Dataverse, external systems or custom instrumentation. Review those destinations separately.

For the documented inbound-agent consent feature, configure and publish the consent topic from Conversation Start and enable Request for User Consent on the workstream. The toggle alone does not make the caller hear a prompt. Test decline, silence and escalation; the sample can treat no input as implicit consent.

Secure external-contact configuration is another control. When available, choose whether Consult and Bridged transfer inherit recording, stop audio only or stop both audio and transcription. Caller consent does not replace a payment-contact capture restriction.

notes.title: Choose the correct SIP metadata mechanism before transferring
notes.body:
Keep SIP UUI and X-headers distinct. The documented external-transfer UUI field is static restricted text and requires Direct Routing egress. It is not a place to insert a runtime expression.

For X-headers, configure Direct Routing and parse Conversation.SipXHeader with the expected schema. Incoming names need a lowercase x- prefix even when the sender uses X-. Update the schema when names change. Outgoing X-header entries on an External phone number transfer can use variables. Test the receiving system’s expected names, supported characters and length limits rather than copying a UUI assumption into this mechanism.

notes.title: Configure real-time voice with explicit voice and turn-taking choices
notes.body:
Author the real-time agent in Copilot Studio and deploy through Contact Center’s telephony integration. Choosing Real-time is one-way for that agent: create another agent if Basic is required later. Confirm model, region and language support for the actual deployment.

Select the agent voice in Copilot Studio; the connected agent does not take a replacement voice from the admin-center setting. Tune turn-taking deliberately. Server-based voice activity detection uses audio silence, while semantic detection considers sentence meaning and can suit callers who hesitate during longer explanations. Validate with representative callers and background conditions rather than assuming one setting fits every journey.

notes.title: Test voice handoff and every authored language path
notes.body:
Use the appropriate system topic and Transfer conversation node for explicit handoff to the connected engagement hub. A spoken announcement that a representative will join is not the transfer action itself. Confirm both the human notification and the context received.

Add supported secondary languages and supply translated strings for authored topics; generated language capability does not translate every maintained message. Keep localization files synchronized when primary text changes. If the voice language region changes, republish and review the speech/TTS configuration. Test voice recognition, consent, keypad prompts and handoff in each intended language rather than relying on a successful text-only preview.

notes.title: Design the queue pool and assignment policy together
notes.body:
Create an advanced queue with the appropriate Messaging, Record or Voice type; that type controls which workstreams can target it. Add the representatives who should be eligible, then select its assignment method. A queue without the intended membership is not a completed staffing configuration.

Queue priority governs competition between queues: a smaller number is higher priority. It is different from a work item's priority within a queue. Highest capacity favors the eligible representative with the most available capacity; advanced round robin rotates eligible representatives, and least active favors the least active eligible person. Decide the business policy before choosing the method, while preserving skill, presence and capacity conditions for the selected configuration.

notes.title: Treat fallback, overflow and opening hours as different controls
notes.body:
Fallback is a workstream safety net for a classification error, route-to-queue error or no matching queue rule. Configure a real fallback queue and its representatives. When a work item reaches it for those reasons, its overflow settings are ignored. Overflow instead applies configured channel-specific condition/action pairs around an otherwise selected queue.

Distinguish the initial prequeue check from waiting-time handling after queueing. For example, out-of-hours handling is an initial condition; prolonged actual waiting can trigger a later queue transfer. Do not assume that every channel supports the same actions.

Create the operating-hours record, choose its timezone and recurrence, add holidays, then associate it with the queue or channel. Daylight saving is handled for the selected timezone. A queue without configured hours is considered available around the clock. Test an actual holiday and after-hours arrival, including its chosen overflow action.

notes.title: Connect self-service to a deliberately configured workstream
notes.body:
Choose the workstream type and Push or Pick distribution when creating it. The distribution mode cannot be edited later, and voice uses Push only. Configure capacity, allowed presences and the channel entry point as a connected design.

For the course's engagement-agent pattern, first configure a Copilot Studio agent and connect it to omnichannel. Select that agent in the workstream's Bot area. Author its escalation behavior in Copilot Studio; the workstream association is not a substitute for a working handoff topic. Collected customer context can then inform classification after escalation.

Classification rules add requirements and attributes before queue selection. Use a linked template when its maintained definition should be reused; choose Copy from template when this workstream needs an editable variation. Test self-service resolution and escalation separately, including whether the handed-off context supports the intended routing.

notes.title: Prepare skill metadata before adding prediction
notes.body:
Build a rating model, skill types and skills, then assign representative proficiency. Attach the work item's required skills through logical classification or a published prediction model. The rating model used for a skill in classification must match the one used for that representative skill; inconsistent scales can break assignment.

Intelligent skill finder uses an AI Builder category classification model. Check regional availability and the documented AI Builder preview-model prerequisite. Select useful text attributes, load the training data, review and approve labels, train and publish. Test predicted tags against skills that actually exist in the organization; a plausible tag is not automatically a valid skill record.

Then include the model in machine-learning classification. Continue checking representative corrections and retrain with reviewed data. Prediction supplies work requirements; the queue's assignment strategy still decides who receives the work. A training result alone is not an end-to-end routing test.

notes.title: Separate intent requirements from preferred-person exceptions
notes.body:
The current intent-driven routing documentation is explicitly preview. Enable Customer Intent Agent and intent discovery, and configure the appropriate Copilot agent on the workstream. The upstream agent determines live chat/voice intent and persists its fields during handoff. Classification can attach skills from intent; queue rules can test intent, intent group or line of business. Unified routing does not itself infer live chat or voice intent from raw messages in this flow.

Standard preferred representative routing serves another goal: a known contact's relationship with selected representatives. Map contacts to representatives who belong to the target queue and use a Push workstream. Allowed presence is checked, but this preferred path skips skills, capacity and ordinary assignment-rule checks. Choose the unavailable-preferred fallback deliberately: next-best assignment or remaining unassigned.

Do not assume a preferred-person configuration enforces the same eligibility contract as standard skill-based assignment. Current intent-driven preview and separate orchestration playbooks also should not be mixed with legacy intent-to-user-group mapping instructions.

notes.title: Use intake rules when moving from basic case routing to unified records
notes.body:
Basic routing rulesets in Customer Service route cases. Create ordered condition/action items, activate the ruleset and test matching cases. The first matching item routes the case and stops further evaluation. Deactivate a ruleset before editing it.

Unified record routing has a broader pipeline. Enable the record type for routing, create a Record workstream and configure intake rules that select its workstream or an active basic routing rule. Those intake conditions are not route-to-queue rules: they choose which routing path receives the record before classification and assignment.

After enabling unified routing, an existing active basic rule does not route records until intake rules are configured. Test the transition in a development environment. Confirm representative record access, not only queue membership; unified assignment cannot grant permission to the underlying record.

notes.title: Diagnose the routing stage that actually failed
notes.body:
Set up conversation diagnostics and its connection to Azure Application Insights before expecting lifecycle evidence. The current setup requires a Managed environment and appropriate Azure and application permissions. This conversation-lifecycle experience replaces reliance on deprecated legacy routing diagnostics; it does not create historical evidence for events that were never collected.

Use the conversation identifier and timestamps to follow Intake, Classification, RouteToQueue and CSRAssignment. Queue selection is not the same as a representative accepting work. When the target queue is correct but work remains unassigned, inspect assignment attempts and the associated snapshot of queue configuration, rules, representative presence, capacity and skills.

Change the failing layer based on evidence. A queue-routing success is no reason to rewrite classification if the assignment snapshot shows an eligibility failure. Conversely, changing representative capacity cannot repair a record that entered the wrong workstream. Keep any query scoped to the relevant conversation and attempt.

notes.title: Assign a workspace experience and shape the inbox for its users
notes.body:
Create a custom experience profile for the team and configure its pane tools, templates and channels. Assign the intended users and verify which profile they receive; an unassigned user gets a supplied default experience. Treat visible tools and permission checks as separate rollout checks.

Enable the inbox and build views around record types and work scope. Use simple filters when they meet the requirement, or advanced conversation conditions for a more specific view. Check Representative visibility and test with the assigned user. An administrator’s successful view configuration is not proof that every representative sees that view.

notes.title: Set template behavior through the relevant configuration layer
notes.body:
Choose the application tab’s page type and parameters deliberately. For an existing entity record, validateRecord prevents an unmatched ID from opening a create form. Choose a Generic session template for channel association or an Entity template for the intended user-owned table. Keep that session structure separate from notification display.

A notification template controls the request presented to the representative. Show timeout changes timer visibility; it does not extend the countdown. Test a missing record, a normal session and an unanswered notification so configuration errors do not become accidental create forms or misleading acceptance expectations.

notes.title: Keep script order and macro record context explicit
notes.body:
Use the script-step Order field for the intended display sequence and resolve dynamic text with the supported slug syntax. Associate the script with its session template. Guidance and execution remain separate: a text instruction does not perform a macro’s data operation.

For macro inputs, distinguish the session anchor from the currently focused tab. Opening an additional account tab does not replace the anchor case context. Use Session.CurrentTab entity identity when the operation intentionally targets that tab, then obtain other values with supported queries. Test macros after switching tabs so automation does not act on a valid but unintended record.

notes.title: Register productivity tools and enable collaboration for the intended profile
notes.body:
Build and publish a custom page or PCF control before registering a pane tool. Registration makes it available for configuration; enable it in the relevant experience profile before expecting representatives to see it. Custom tools do not automatically receive the current session’s context, so design that integration explicitly.

For Teams collaboration, check the app’s Teams-chat settings, the user’s custom profile and the required permissions. Connecting a chat to a record helps colleagues keep the discussion together, but it does not grant access to the record. Test with the actual representative and collaborator identities rather than only an administrator account.

notes.title: Use the API that owns the workspace or conversation operation
notes.body:
Use the app profile manager API for sessions, tabs and session context. Check canCreateSession or canCreateTab before attempting another UI container, and verify API role prerequisites. An opened tab is a workspace navigation result.

Use the Omnichannel JavaScript API for conversation operations such as retrieving its ID or linking an account, contact or case. Confirm the focused session before linking because that operation targets its conversation. Keep this representative-side SDK separate from the customer-facing widget SDK. Test a session switch before performing the action so navigation success is not mistaken for a correct conversation association. Record linking here is scoped to standalone Contact Center or the documented Customer Service workspace; Link to conversation is not applicable to the embedded Contact Center experience.

notes.title: Prepare the table and search surface for internal knowledge
notes.body:
Enable knowledge management for the intended record type and configure the relevant search surface. In the workspace, enable the side pane and knowledge search in the assigned experience profile. Set up Dataverse search and the Knowledge Article Quick Find columns, including Content, so the intended fields participate in discovery. Keep article privileges aligned with the user’s duties.

Match control placement to the app. The form-control procedure is scoped to single-session apps or non-anchor auto-search; multisession apps use the knowledge search control on the app side pane. Validate discovery with a representative record and a known article rather than assuming successful control placement establishes useful search.

notes.title: Configure external discovery and public links as separate integrations
notes.body:
Add an external search provider for the intended source and verify access to that source with the representative identity. A provider record does not authorize external content. Keep federated search distinct from selecting knowledge sources for a generative agent.

For customer-facing article links, create the portal and configure Use an external portal with the documented URL format. The kbnum placeholder resolves to the article’s public number. Enable attachment synchronization separately if required. Test the resulting link and attachments as an intended external reader; a working internal search result does not demonstrate a working public article page.

notes.title: Separate knowledge harvesting from publication approval
notes.body:
Prepare knowledge management, Copilot knowledge access and the required connection references. Enable the associated flows and publish the knowledge-harvest agent. For real-time creation, configure rules for resolved cases or closed conversations; the agent compares existing knowledge before deciding that a new article is needed.

Choose publication governance separately. A Pending compliance state can support reviewer approval, while automatic publication depends on compliant status and the selected internal or internal-and-external audience. The product warns that sensitive-data removal can miss content, so inspect generated material before broad publication. Test creation, review and the intended audience rather than treating a generated draft as an approved public article.

notes.title: Enable the specific supervisor intervention before testing it
notes.body:
In Contact Center standalone, access to a dashboard and permission to act are different checks. Configure the Monitor, Assign, Transfer and Force Close switches in Ongoing conversation insights for the interventions the supervisor is authorized to use. Keep analytics report/data access separate from these action switches.

Then test with a conversation in the appropriate state. Assignment targets an Open, unassigned conversation; transfer addresses supported Active or Waiting messaging conversations between representatives. Elevated voice/video and AI-agent endpoints have their own restrictions. Force Close immediately ends the interaction, so it is not a substitute for resolving a routine assignment problem. These settings establish the documented workspace supervisor experience; they do not establish a separate new app's rollout or availability.

notes.title: Prepare quality evaluation dependencies and choose the right plan
notes.body:
Use the conversation-evaluation framework deliberately. Criteria contain questions, scoring and guidance; a plan selects interactions, timing and criteria; evaluations are the resulting assessments. Set up the documented quality roles, Copilot credits, AI enablement and regional-data consent before testing the framework. Check that connection references, flows and the published Copilot Studio agent show ready.

For future qualifying conversations, configure a Conversations plan with a closed-conversation trigger. Recurring and once-only plans address other review schedules. Add conditions and evaluation criteria, then save and activate the plan. Check results against the intended population instead of assuming that creating criteria starts evaluation. This note teaches conversation evaluation; it does not imply that every record type or preview option is universally available.

notes.title: Choose visual editing only when the existing metrics answer the question
notes.body:
For a standalone analytics report, begin by deciding whether the data already contains the required metric. The embedded editor can change charts, layouts, filters and available measures. Save and publish intentionally: the published customization is visible to the organization, not merely a private bookmark. Reset removes those customizations permanently.

A new business calculation is a different requirement. Use data-model customization when the existing model lacks the needed logic or data, rather than trying to change a KPI's meaning by renaming its visual. Reuse supported out-of-the-box metrics where they already fit, and define only the organization-specific additions. Keep a reviewable distinction between a new presentation and a new calculation.

notes.title: Extend the managed model without treating custom reports as an operations console
notes.body:
Scope: Contact Center standalone reporting.

Enable historical or real-time model customization, provision the models and report copies, and connect Power BI Desktop to the appropriate model in the managed workspace. Use supported fields and measures. For additional attributes or external data, build a local composite model and relationships instead of directly changing the managed dataset. Treat that managed dataset as read-only because service updates maintain it.

Publish the report to the customer workspace and arrange the required model/report permissions. Report copies and your custom extensions need their own maintenance as the source model evolves. Model-customized reports are analytical surfaces: supervisor assign, transfer, monitor and force-close actions are not available there. Retain the operational conversation report for those interventions.

notes.title: Embed the correct reporting surface and verify its access path
notes.body:
Scope: Contact Center standalone reporting.

Built-in analytics reports are embedded in Copilot Service workspace navigation. Enable the required analytics feature and user access rather than assuming a separate Power BI browser session is the only way to read them. In a customized workspace app, the documented report-table content configuration can preserve report state across session tabs.

Custom model reports follow another publication path. After publishing to the configured customer workspace, add the report in the historical or real-time model customization page and save it into the shared Customized Reports navigation. The report picker uses that configured workspace. Check model permissions, report/workspace access and embedding settings together; a valid report in a different workspace does not automatically appear in that picker. Current commercial licensing requirements should be checked separately.

notes.title: Distinguish collecting diagnostic events from displaying them in Dynamics
notes.body:
Configure the Managed environment's conversation diagnostics and Application Insights export with the documented Azure and Power Platform permissions. Ingestion and query access are separate responsibilities. Verify that lifecycle events reach the intended instance before diagnosing a workspace display problem; event telemetry complements conversation recordings and transcripts rather than replacing them.

The Diagnose Debug experience needs additional setup. Supply the Application Insights ID in its Dataverse environment variable, register the application and federated credentials, update the managed identity information, and grant the app Monitoring Reader access. Enable the Application Insights Dashboard app setting at both default and environment-value levels. Then validate the embedded Debug tab. Successful export alone does not establish Dataverse's authorization to read and display that telemetry.

cards.prompt: Which Contact Center component brings representative conversations into a non-Microsoft CRM?
cards.answer: The embedded conversation widget.
cards.explanation: It supports hosting the representative experience in a suitable HTML/JavaScript application.

cards.prompt: Which security role does the Contact Center workspace overview require for a representative?
cards.answer: Omnichannel Agent.
cards.explanation: This is the documented prerequisite for using Copilot Service workspace.

cards.prompt: How should a development solution be packaged when deploying Contact Center configuration to production?
cards.answer: Author it unmanaged in development, then export it as managed for production.
cards.explanation: This preserves a controlled deployment boundary.

cards.prompt: Does restoring a Contact Center environment finish all omnichannel recovery work?
cards.answer: No. Follow up with channel provisioning or unified-routing enablement as applicable.
cards.explanation: The restored environment still needs the documented service setup steps.

cards.prompt: A managed configuration update imports successfully into a target with matching installed solution versions. The imported package contains the intended change, but a record previously edited directly in the target still shows its old customization. What should you investigate?
cards.answer: An active customization layer overriding the managed layer.
cards.explanation: Investigate the target-side active customization: it can take precedence over the incoming managed configuration. The scenario rules out a failed import, version mismatch, and an omitted source change.

options.text: The target record's active customization layer.
A failed solution import that prevented the package from arriving.
Different installed solution versions between source and target.
A source change omitted from the exported package.

cards.prompt: After migrating skill-based routing configuration, which target-side follow-up does Microsoft explicitly require where skills and ratings are used?
cards.answer: Link, associate, or create the relevant users, bookable resources, and characteristics.
cards.explanation: Ruleset rendering is one verification step, but skills and ratings also require user, bookable-resource, and characteristic associations. Capacity-profile associations address a separate configuration; reimporting definitions alone does not perform the required association check.

options.text: Verify only that the imported routing rulesets render without errors.
Associate only resource capacity-profile records, leaving skill characteristics unlinked.
Link or create the users, resources, and characteristics.
Reimport the skill definitions without checking their target resource associations.

cards.prompt: Does linking a visitor to a contact through a preconversation email address authenticate the visitor?
cards.answer: No. Record identification is not authentication.
cards.explanation: Authenticated chat verifies a signed token from the website's sign-in flow.

cards.prompt: What naming rule matters when an integration supplies a workstream context variable?
cards.answer: The supplied name must match exactly, including letter case.
cards.explanation: Keep the defined name consistent across the integration.

cards.prompt: What happens to workstream context when a preconversation survey question is added?
cards.answer: A corresponding context variable is created.
cards.explanation: Inspect it under the workstream's advanced context-variable settings.

cards.prompt: Where does the documented website integration place a chat instance's widget snippet?
cards.answer: Inside the website's HTML body.
cards.explanation: Copy the snippet from that chat instance's Chat widget tab.

cards.prompt: A preconversation lookup finds two active contacts with the same supplied email. What automatic-linking outcome should you expect?
cards.answer: No automatic customer link is made from the ambiguous match.
cards.explanation: The lookup does not choose the oldest, newest, or first returned matching record.

options.text: The oldest contact is linked.
No record is automatically linked from that match.
The first returned contact is linked.
The newest contact is linked.

cards.prompt: A developer wants to delete a workstream context variable. What should be checked first?
cards.answer: Whether classification or assignment rules use it.
cards.explanation: Microsoft specifically requires checking unified-routing classification and assignment dependencies before a necessary update or deletion. Survey, website, or AI-agent checks can be useful, but none alone establishes that routing rules no longer depend on the variable.

options.text: Inspect only whether a preconversation survey displays the variable.
Inspect only the website custom-context provider code.
Inspect only the variable names used by the AI agent.
Whether classification or assignment rules reference it.

cards.prompt: Which conversation types can Copilot summarize in standalone Contact Center?
cards.answer: Chat and transcribed voice conversations.
cards.explanation: The conversation-summary setup targets a conversation recap, distinct from a case summary.

cards.prompt: Where can a representative find a saved summary for a closed conversation?
cards.answer: Open the conversation from Activities and use its Summary tab.
cards.explanation: The closed conversation remains a place to review its generated recap.

cards.prompt: Which Copilot filter lets representatives choose knowledge filters themselves in Ask a question?
cards.answer: A representative filter.
cards.explanation: Enable its filter status so it appears in the help pane.

cards.prompt: Does a Copilot Studio global variable retain its value across all future customer sessions?
cards.answer: No. Its scope spans topics within one user session.
cards.explanation: A global variable is session-scoped, not permanent customer storage; clearing or resetting variables can also remove its value.

cards.prompt: Copilot is configured and all representatives have the required security privileges. Only the escalation team should receive the selected Copilot features. Which configuration should define that team's feature access?
cards.answer: Enable the selected features in a custom experience profile and assign it to that team.
cards.explanation: Experience profiles determine the Copilot features available to assigned representatives. A shared default profile does not isolate the team; recording captures interactions, and knowledge filters restrict response content rather than feature access.

options.text: Enable the selected features in a custom experience profile and assign it to that team.
Enable the features in the default experience profile assigned to every representative.
Enable recording of Copilot interactions for the escalation team.
Apply a preset knowledge filter for the team's subject area.

cards.prompt: A native standalone voice agent needs the caller's phone number in several topics. Where should it first copy Activity.From.Name?
cards.answer: Into a global variable in Conversation Start.
